heading: INT. GOLDEN LOTUS NAIL SALON - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. GOLDEN LOTUS NAIL SALON - AFTERNOON
The salon is narrow and too warm, a corridor of pedicure chairs under a wall of lacquer bottles arranged by colour like a slow sunset.
Acetone hangs in the air, sweet and chemical, and a muted television in the corner plays a court reporter's silent mouth over footage of a courthouse.
Beneath it all runs the steady tick of a wall clock that is four minutes fast.
Marisol Vega, 40s, a public defender in a creased navy suit, sits with her hands spread on the table like something she is trying to keep from escaping.
She has not slept.
The exhaustion has made her very still, and stillness is how she has learned to look calm.
Across from her, doing her nails, is Quinn Alder, 20s, who wears a name tag that says QUINN and a quiet, careful expression.
Quinn is nonbinary, uses they and them, and has a way of listening that makes people say more than they planned.
They file one nail, then another, never rushing.
By the door, a WOMAN in a grey trench coat, sunglasses still on despite the indoors, has taken the waiting chair.
She holds a paper cup of tea she does not drink.
She has been there eleven minutes.
Nobody has asked what she wants.
You have court tomorrow?
units.name: QUINN

units.text: Closing arguments. If I'm honest I'd rather be anywhere else.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Then why here?
units.name: QUINN

units.text: Because last night I realised my hands were shaking and I didn't want the jury to see it.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Quinn smiles, small, and lifts her index finger to the light.
They won't. Not with this colour.
units.name: QUINN

units.text: The woman in the trench coat sets down her tea.
The cup makes a flat plastic click against the table, and both of them look over.
Ms. Vega.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Marisol does not turn her head.
This is the thing she has trained herself to do for twenty years: when the worst arrives, let it come to you.
You're not supposed to be here.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Neither are you.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Do you two know each other?
units.name: QUINN

units.text: No.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Yes.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: They speak across each other, and Quinn looks from one to the other, the file still held in mid-air.
My name is Dolores Reyes. My son is the man you're about to call a liar tomorrow morning.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Mrs. Reyes, you are a witness's mother. If you're talking to me you are violating the court's order. Please leave.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: He's twenty-three.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Please leave.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: He told the police the truth and you are going to stand up in front of twelve strangers and say it was a story.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Excuse me. I think maybe everyone should breathe.
units.name: QUINN

units.text: Quinn, don't.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Don't tell them not to. They're the only one in this room not afraid of me.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: This is the last time any of them will be calm in this room.
Marisol stands.
The chair legs SCRAPE the tile, and every head in the salon turns, the manicurists, the customers, the blank face of the television.
I am doing my job.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Your job is a knife.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: It is a promise. To a man who will go to prison for life if I don't.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: And my son?
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Is not on trial.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Then why does it feel like he is?
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Dolores throws the paper cup.
It hits the wall of lacquer, and a dozen bottles tumble, SHATTERING across the floor in red and violet and pearl.
The smell of acetone doubles, sharp enough to sting.
Quinn steps between them, both hands raised, polish brush still dripping onto their glove.
Stop. Both of you. Please.
units.name: QUINN

units.text: Nobody moves.
A single bottle rolls, slowly, until it comes to rest against Marisol's shoe.
